data.input:
Our style guide requires typographic (curly) quotation marks in published prose. In NOTES.md, change only the tagline line so it reads exactly:

Tagline: “Fast” and ‘simple’

Use the curly characters “ ” ‘ ’ (U+201C, U+201D, U+2018, U+2019), not straight quotes. Do not change any other line.

rawInput.command:
cat -A /workspace/project/NOTES.md; echo '---'; python3 -c "
import unicodedata
for line in open('/workspace/project/NOTES.md'):
    print([hex(ord(c)) for c in line.strip() if not c.isascii()], repr(line))
"

cat -A /workspace/project/NOTES.md; echo '---'; python3 -c "

"

rawInput.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p = '/workspace/project/NOTES.md'
with open(p, encoding='utf-8') as f:
    lines = f.read().split('\n')
assert lines[2].startswith('Tagline:'), lines[2]
# literal backslash-escaped unicode to avoid tool-layer normalization
lines[2] = 'Tagline: \u201cFast\u201d and \u2018simple\u2019'
with open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write('\n'.join(lines))
EOF
python3 -c "
for line in open('/workspace/project/NOTES.md', encoding='utf-8'):
    print(repr(line), [hex(ord(c)) for c in line if not c.isascii()])
"
